Kalinjar fell on 27 April 1203 ('the fort's garrison surrendered') and Trailokyavarman was Kalanjaradhipati again in 1205; the hold is drawn as a hatched occupation from the ledger. unverified: page budget for the Baghelkhand cells. ledger.note: c. 831: Nannuka founds the Chandela kingdom around Khajuraho. Infobox 'Founded: c. 831'; Nannuka 'the founder of the dynasty, was the ruler of a small kingdom centered around Khajuraho' (reign 831-845). A Pratihara vassal at first. Region cut from 80 to 50 km in the repair of 2026-10-19: the 80 km disc held Kalinjar (59 km away), which the Kalinjar Fort page has under the Pratiharas by 836 and taken from the Kalachuris only 'before 954'.

ledger.note: 836 (bridge; the Pratihara dossier's year, Mihira Bhoja's accession): the Chandelas rule as Pratihara vassals. 'The Chandelas initially ruled as feudatories of the Gurjara-Pratiharas' (no year); Harsha (r. c. 905-925) 'played an important role in restoring the rule of the Pratihara king Mahipala'; Yashovarman (c. 925-950) 'continued to acknowledge the Pratihara suzerainty, but became practically independent'. The Gurjara-Pratihara page lists the Chandelas of Bundelkhand among the feudatories of the empire. Mirror of gurjara-pratihara-dynasty /ledger/18. Region: the K0 district (the Pratihara dossier tints all of Bundelkhand outside the Doab, Gwalior and Malwa). Added in the repair of 2026-10-19 (reviewer finding).

region.text: a small kingdom centered around Khajuraho (50 km, so that Kalinjar, 59 km away, lies outside)

ledger.note: c. 950: Dhanga formally founds Chandela sovereignty. 'Dhanga (r. c. 950-999) ... his records do not mention any Pratihara overlord. This indicates that Dhanga formally established the Chandela sovereignty.' Yashovarman 'continued to acknowledge the Pratihara suzerainty, but became practically independent'. The Gurjara-Pratihara page puts the feudatories' break-away under Mahipala I (912-944), without a year for the Chandelas. Mirror of gurjara-pratihara-dynasty /ledger/30 (c. 950). Added 2026-10-19.

c. 950: the Chandelas take Gwalior. Gurjara-Pratihara page: 'the Chandelas captured the strategic fortress of Gwalior in central India around 950.' (The Chandela page does not credit Yashovarman or Dhanga with Gwalior; it has the Kachchhapaghatas of Gwalior as Chandela subordinates who 'probably gave up their allegiance' under Vijayapala, c. 1035-1050.) Mirror of gurjara-pratihara-dynasty /ledger/31. Added 2026-10-19 (reviewer finding): no Chandela keyframe drew Gwalior (the 960 shape starts at 78.82 E, Gwalior is at 78.18 E).

region.text: Cliopatria's 960 shape beyond the Khajuraho district and Kalinjar (Bundelkhand and the Doab margin)

ledger.note: c. 950 (bridge): the rest of Cliopatria's 960 shape (Bundelkhand and the Doab margin) beyond the home district and Kalinjar. Moved from 960 to 950 in the repair of 2026-10-19: Dhanga's accession (c. 950), the start of keyframe 950 and the end of the Pratihara vassalage. The page: Dhanga 'formally established the Chandela sovereignty'; Khajuraho inscriptions say Kosala, Kuntala and others 'listened humbly to the commands of Dhanga's officers', which the page calls exaggeration. Page silent on the limits; the extent is Cliopatria's 960 shape.

region.text: Kalinjar (Kalanjara), the hill fort, beyond the Khajuraho district

ledger.note: By 954: Yashovarman holds Kalinjar. 'Sometime before 954, the Chandela dynasty under Yashovarman had captured Kalinjar from the Kalachuris'; the Chandela page: Yashovarman 'conquered the important fortress of Kalanjara' and the 953-954 Khajuraho inscription credits him with successes against the Chedis (the Kalachuris of Tripuri), 'exaggerated'. Kalinjar Fort page reread 2026-10-19: 'Sometime before 954, the Chandela dynasty under Yashovarman had captured Kalinjar from the Kalachuris'; 'By the year 836, Kalinjar appears to have been under Gurjara-Pratihara control' and the fort then 'changed several times in the mid-900s'. The Chandela page's Yashovarman reign ends 950, so the capture may be earlier; 954 is the page's bound.

c. 1035 (bridge): Gwalior leaves the Chandela sphere. 'The Kachchhapaghatas of Gwalior probably gave up their allegiance to the Chandelas during this period' (Vijayapala, r. c. 1035-1050; the page gives no year). Added 2026-10-19 to close the Gwalior gain of 950.

region.text: the eastern parts of the Chandela kingdom, toward Baghelkhand (the page names no place)

ledger.note: c. 1035: the Kalachuris conquer eastern parts. At the end of Vidyadhara's reign (1003-1035): 'the Ghaznavid invasions had weakened the Chandela kingdom' and the Kalachuri king Gangeya-deva 'conquered eastern parts of the kingdom'. Vidyadhara had paid tribute to Mahmud of Ghazni ('later invaded'; Kalinjar page: 1023). The page gives no place.

region.text: the eastern parts of the Chandela kingdom, toward Baghelkhand (the page names no place)

ledger.note: c. 1070: Kirttivarman wins the east back. 'His younger brother Kirttivarman resurrected the Chandela power by defeating Lakshmi-Karna' (reign 1060-1100); Kirttivarman page (opened 2026-10-19): 'S. K. Mitra dates the battle to c. 1070 CE.' The first version used his accession, 1060 (confidence 1). The page names no place for the battle or the lands, so the region is the same disc as the 1035 loss; the Ajaygadh inscription says he 'created a new kingdom' by defeating Karna.

region.text: the northern edge that Cliopatria's 1085 shape drops

ledger.note: 1085 (bridge): 28 cells on the northern edge pass to the Gahadavalas, whose Cliopatria row begins in 1085. The page names no place or year ('friendly relations with his northern neighbours'). Gahadavala page reread 2026-10-19: it does not mention the Chandelas; it has Chandradeva independent 'sometime before 1089/1090' (infobox 'Established: 1072'). The 1085 year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the six north-eastern cells (25.0-26.0 N, 80.3-81.5 E) that Cliopatria's 1152 shape adds

ledger.note: 1152 (bridge; Cliopatria's year): northern Baghelkhand. Madanavarman page: he 'may have annexed the northern part of the Baghelkhand region' (no year; reign c. 1128-1165); Chandela page: he 'defeated the Kalachuri king Gaya-Karna, and possibly annexed the northern part of the Baghelkhand region. However, the Chandelas lost this territory to Gaya-Karna's successor Narasimha.' Narasimha's inscriptions at Lal Pahadi (1158) and Alhaghat (1159) in the region show that 'the Chandelas could not retain this territory for long', so the shapes that keep these cells to 1315 are unverified. Added 2026-10-19 (thin finding).

region.text: Jejakabhukti, the Chandela country, and Mahoba

ledger.note: c. 1182-83: Prithviraj Chauhan invades. 'the Chahamana ruler Prithviraj Chauhan invaded the Chandela kingdom' and 'sacked Mahoba'; the Madanpur inscriptions of 1182-83 corroborate the raid. No annexation (Talbot) or a short one (R. B. Singh, Prithviraj page).

region.text: Jejakabhukti, the Chandela country, and Mahoba

ledger.note: 1183: the raid ends; Paramardi remains king. The Chandela page has no peace; the Prithviraj page: 'Prithviraj was not able to annex the Chandela territory'.

region.text: the 24 cells of northern Baghelkhand (24.0-25.7 N, 80.9-82.7 E) that Cliopatria's 1202 shape adds

ledger.note: 1202 (bridge; Cliopatria's year): 24 more cells of northern Baghelkhand. No page dates a Chandela return to the region after Narasimha's inscriptions of 1158-1159 (Madanavarman page), so the growth is unexplained by a page; the cells stay as Cliopatria draws them. A gap-filler should check the Kalachuri (Tripuri) side. Added 2026-10-19 (thin finding).

27 April 1203: Aibak takes Kalinjar. 'This period of prosperity was interrupted in 1202 or 1203' when Qutb ud-Din Aibak besieged the fort; Paramardi 'apparently surrendered and offered tribute' and died; 'Finally, on 27 April 1203, the fort's garrison surrendered.' Hatched, not annexed: the Chandela page has Aibak invade c. 1202-1203 and Paramardi surrender but does not say he took Kalanjara.
By 1205: the Chandelas retake Kalinjar. 'A 1205 inscription refers to Trailokyavarman with the title Kalanjaradhipati once again'; he reconquered the fort 'within a couple of years'.

1315: the Chandela kingdom ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1315'; Viravarman II (1311-1315) was the last of the table. The page dates no Delhi conquest; Cliopatria's row ends in 1313. Kalinjar Fort page reread 2026-10-19: no sentence on the Khalji, Alauddin or the Delhi Sultanate, and no 14th-century year; the end remains the Chandela infobox's 1315.

wars.name: Ghaznavid invasions of the Chandela kingdom
wars.outcome: Vidyadhara 'killed the king of Kannauj (possibly Rajyapala) for fleeing his capital instead of fighting the Ghaznavid invader'; 'Mahmud later invaded Vidyadhara's kingdom', which 'ended with Vidyadhara paying tribute to Mahmud' (Muslim sources). The Kalinjar page: 'In 1023, Mahmud of Ghazni attacked and received a tribute from Kalinjar'. No land changed hands; the tribute is the Ghaznavid dossier's vassal tint.

the northern Baghelkhand that Madanavarman possibly annexed

wars.outcome: Gangeya-deva took the eastern parts; Lakshmi-Karna subjugated Devavarman; Kirttivarman defeated Lakshmi-Karna (1060-1100); Madanavarman defeated Gaya-Karna and possibly annexed northern Baghelkhand, lost to Narasimha (undated).

wars.name: Chandela-Paramara wars
wars.outcome: Sallakshanavarman raided the Paramaras; Naravarman lost territory to the Chandelas (Paramara page); Madanavarman captured the Bhilsa territory, recaptured by Lakshmivarman (undated).

wars.name: Chaulukya-Chandela conflict
wars.outcome: Jayasimha 'reached as far as the Chandela kingdom'; the conflict 'appears to have been inconclusive, as records of both the kingdoms claim victory'.

wars.name: Prithviraj III-Chandela war (Mahoba)

zones.text: Jejakabhukti, the Chandela country, and Mahoba

wars.outcome: Prithviraj invaded and sacked Mahoba in 1182-83 without a lasting annexation.

wars.name: Ghurid conquest of Kalinjar
wars.outcome: Aibak besieged Kalinjar in 1202 or 1203; the garrison surrendered on 27 April 1203; Trailokyavarman had the fort again by 1205.

wars.name: Ghurid expedition against Kalinjar
wars.outcome: A commander's expedition of 1233/34 plundered the town below the fort; 'Taisi does not appear to have actually captured the fortress'.

certainty.note: No treaty line appears on any page opened. The Chandela realm is known from inscriptions and from the sites of its forts (Khajuraho, Kalanjara, Mahoba); its limits with the Kalachuris, Paramaras and Gahadavalas are approximate.

notes:
Settled from pages: founding c. 831 around Khajuraho, Kalinjar held before 954, the Kalachuri conquest of the eastern parts at the end of Vidyadhara's reign and its reversal under Kirttivarman, the Prithviraj raid of 1182-83, Kalinjar taken on 27 April 1203 and back by 1205, the end in 1315.
Disagreements: (1) The Kalinjar page says Aibak took Kalinjar in 1203; the Chandela page says only that he invaded c. 1202-1203 and Paramardi surrendered. (2) The infobox names the Ghurid dynasty and the Mamluk dynasty (Delhi) as successors although no page records a conquest after 1205. (3) The Pratihara dossier has the Chandelas take Gwalior c. 950 (Pratihara page) while the Chandela page has the Kachchhapaghatas of Gwalior as later subordinates (they 'gave up their allegiance' under Vijayapala); Cliopatria's shape does not reach Gwalior (26.2 N 78.2 E). Not drawn.
Not settled: the place and year of the 1035 Kalachuri conquest and of the 1060 recovery (inferred from reign tables; 'eastern parts' is drawn as a 110 km disc at 24.6 N 82.5 E); the Baghelkhand cells of 1152 and 1202; Madanavarman's Bhilsa capture and its recapture (undated); Chaulukya-Chandela inconclusive war (undated). Pages (4 of 5): Chandelas of Jejakabhukti, Kalinjar Fort (the title 'Kalinjar (fort)' failed to load), Jayasimha Siddharaja and Prithviraj Chauhan (both opened for other dossiers of the batch and read again here for the Chaulukya and Mahoba lines). Gazetteer names needed: Khajuraho (24.85 N 79.92 E), Kalinjar (25.00 N 80.48 E), Mahoba (25.29 N 79.87 E), Baghelkhand (region: Rewa and Satna country, 24-25 N, 80.5-82.5 E). Counterparts without dossier: kalachuris-of-tripuri. Tomara/other: none.

Repair 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review of sa-03-f, verdict fail). (1) The Pratihara vassalage is now in the ledger: vassal_start 836 (confidence 1, the Pratihara dossier's year; the Chandela page gives none) and vassal_end c. 950 (confidence 2), counterpart gurjara-pratihara-dynasty, region the K0 district; the Pratihara dossier tints all of Bundelkhand outside the Doab, Gwalior and Malwa for the same years. (2) Gwalior: gain c. 950 from the Pratiharas (Gurjara-Pratihara page: 'the Chandelas captured the strategic fortress of Gwalior ... around 950'; the Chandela and Kalinjar pages say nothing of it) and loss c. 1035 (the Kachchhapaghatas 'probably gave up their allegiance' under Vijayapala; counterpart kachchhapaghatas-of-gwalior, confidence 1). The Chandela page also does not say Gwalior was held directly. (3) The 960 gain moved to 950 and Kalinjar's disc was taken out of K0 (50 km disc) and out of K1 until 954, so the ledger and the keyframes agree. (4) Recovery of the east moved from 1060 to c. 1070 (Kirttivarman page, S. K. Mitra). (5) Baghelkhand: the 6 cells of 1152 and 24 cells of 1202 are confidence-1 bridges; the Madanavarman page shows the Kalachuris (Narasimha) holding the region in 1158-1159 and gives no Chandela return, so these cells are unverified and may be wrong. (6) Newly learned but not drawn: Madanavarman was at Bhilsa (Vidisha) in 1134 (Augasi inscription) and Lakshmivarman recaptured the region by 1143-44; a Paramara-side event pair is open (paramara-dynasty notes). (7) Gahadavala page: no Chandela land mentioned, 1085 stays Cliopatria's year; Khalji end: no page dates it (Kalinjar Fort page: no Khalji sentence). Counterpart needing a dossier: kachchhapaghatas-of-gwalior (c. 950-c. 1035 as Chandela subordinates; not worth a dossier on its own).
